topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic and outlines the approach of synthesizing previously introduced immune components.

topics.label: Recognition of infection and damage via PAMPs and DAMPs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the molecular signals of microbial presence and tissue injury that enable the innate immune system to distinguish self from non-self.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptors and inflammatory signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the genetics, cellular localization, and downstream signaling cascades of pattern recognition receptor families and intracellular inflammasome complexes.

topics.label: Leukocyte recruitment, trafficking, and systemic inflammatory responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mobilization and vascular extravasation of immune cells into tissues, their lymphatic transport, and the pathological consequences of excessive systemic activation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic adaptations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how acute inflammation is terminated, how damaged tissues are repaired, and how the body manages persistent inflammation through chronic structures like granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and announces the subject of the upcoming lecture.
